year.shelter: Hibernates at the bottom of ponds and lakes, or buried under leaves and moss on land; spends summer in damp forest and meadows.
year.young: In April–May each female lays a clump of about 2,000 eggs in a pond; the tadpoles turn into tiny froglets by July.

food.spring: Little: it is busy laying eggs.
food.summer: Insects, spiders, worms and slugs, caught with its sticky tongue.

year.notes: Eaten by pike, foxes, herons, storks and grass snakes. The spring croaking choruses and the frogspawn would be great to show.

text.title: Common frog
text.stalk_hint: A frog! Get close slowly, then tap Pounce before it hops away.
text.about_looks: A smooth brown or olive frog with a dark patch behind each golden eye and long, strong back legs.
text.about_food: Insects, spiders, worms and slugs, caught with a long sticky tongue.
text.about_home: Lives in damp forests and meadows near ponds and lakes, and goes back to the water to lay its eggs.
text.about_winter: Sleeps through winter at the bottom of a pond, or buried under leaves and moss.
text.about_young: Lays big clumps of eggs in ponds in spring. Tadpoles hatch and turn into tiny froglets by summer.
text.about_fact: A frog can breathe through its skin, so it can sleep all winter underwater.
